issue.body:
# Description of Changes

- `pdftohtml` got the upload's base name as a bare positional argument, so a file named `-xml.pdf` / `-stdout.pdf` / `--help.pdf` was read as an option, a long name failed to convert, and the name was written unescaped into the generated HTML. It now always gets the fixed output name `document`, and the input path is absolute. The zip entries in the HTML and Markdown exports are now `document.html`, `document001.png` and so on; the zip itself keeps the upload's name.
- `processPdfToHtml` and `processPdfToOfficeFormat` no longer swallow zip write errors and return a broken zip as a success.
- The `/file/pdf` work dir and the PDF/A LibreOffice output dir now come from `TempFileManager`, so they use the configured temp location and are covered by the periodic cleanup.
- `/file/pdf` now closes the upload's input stream.
- `/convert/file/pdf`: the work dir is now deleted when the LibreOffice conversion or the sanitize step fails.
- `/convert/ebook/pdf`: the working dir (which holds the upload) is now deleted when Calibre fails, since the checks now run inside the try/finally.
- `/convert/pdf/pdfa` (PDFBox/LibreOffice fallback): the LibreOffice output dir is now deleted when the LibreOffice step fails.
- Audited every other `ProcessExecutor` command line (LibreOffice/unoconvert, calibre, gs, qpdf, tesseract/ocrmypdf, weasyprint, ffmpeg, magick, rar). None of them pass a user-controlled argument that can start with `-`: they use absolute temp paths, allowlisted values, or the `--opt=value` form.

Verified against the running backend (`bootRun`, host poppler 26.10 and calibre), before and after, with a generated one-page PDF:

| Request | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/pdf/html` `-xml.pdf` | 200, empty zip (22 B), `stirling-pdf-*.xml` left in the temp root | 200, zip with `document.html`, `document-1.html`, `document_ind.html`, `document001.png` |
| `/pdf/html` `-stdout.pdf` | 200, empty zip, 4 HTML/PNG files left in the temp root | 200, full zip |
| `/pdf/html` `--help.pdf` | 200, empty zip | 200, full zip |
| `/pdf/html` `-q -o x.pdf` / `normal.pdf` | full zip | full zip, entries named `document*` |
| `/file/pdf` with a failing LibreOffice stub | `office2pdf_` dir left behind | none left |
| `/ebook/pdf` with a corrupt `.epub` | working dir with the uploaded `.epub` left behind | none left |
| `/pdf/pdfa` (`pdfa-1`, Ghostscript unavailable) with a failing LibreOffice stub | `output_` dir left behind | none left |

- `/pdf/markdown` no longer uses `pdftohtml` (`PdfMarkdownExtractor`) and `/pdf/epub` passes absolute paths. Both returned correct output for all four names before and after.
- The fixed output name was checked against poppler 24.04 `pdftohtml`: both the HTML (`-c`) and Markdown (`-s -noframes -c`) commands write only `document*` files into the working dir, while a 250-character name fails with `Couldn't open html file`.
- The cleanup tests fail the process by throwing, as the real `ProcessExecutor` does on a non-zero exit.

issue.body:
## Current state

The desktop app ships without the Processor. Its rail entry, the Processor's settings sections and Usage & Billing are hidden, and #8001 sends desktop billing to the web app in the browser.

## Problem

A desktop user signed in to Stirling Cloud or a self-hosted server cannot open the Processor, manage usage and billing, or link a self-hosted server to Stirling Cloud from the app. One desktop build serves both editions, so the web's build-time split (SaaS vs self-hosted bundles) does not fit.

## Solution

- **Processor as a desktop page.** Desktop `Landing` routes `/processor/*` to the Processor inside the editor's providers, so the connection, session and open files survive switching. A new `portal-desktop` layer picks the cloud or server implementation of each Processor seam at runtime from the connection. `ProcessorEditionBoundary` and a per-connection query client drop state when the mode, server or account changes. Hosted seams shared by web SaaS and desktop move from `portal-saas` to `portal-cloud`.
- **Transport.** Processor calls use the connected server's absolute URL through the native client. The Processor's app config comes from that server.
- **Access.** Stirling Cloud asks `/auth/me` per account; self-hosted reads the session. Without access the Processor sends the user to the editor; local mode asks them to sign in.
- **Settings.** Users, API keys, Audit, Encryption, Usage & Billing and Account link, per edition (Users is admin-only on self-hosted, as in #8316). Usage & Billing replaces the old cloud Plan page and #8001's browser handoff.
- **Billing.** Stripe pages open in the system browser and come back through a new web page, `/desktop/return`, which deep-links to `stirlingpdf://billing/return`. Desktop requests hosted checkout. Licensing and Team checkout use the Stirling Cloud project the app signs in to.
- **Linking a self-hosted server in one go.** The admin signs in to Stirling Cloud inside the app (Google or GitHub via the existing Rust OAuth, or email and password). The app approves the server's connect request as that account, completes it on the server, and keeps the tokens as the billing session. No callback page is involved.
- **Default view on launch** gains "Processor" on desktop for accounts with access.
- **Shell.** The Processor's search sits in the title-bar strip. Editor tool hotkeys and Ctrl+S stay quiet on Processor pages. An OS file-open lands in the editor. External links go through the platform seams.
- **Web fixes found on the way.** Opening a Stripe page in a new tab also navigated the current page (`window.open` with `noopener` returns null). Onboarding's "open the Processor" pointed at the retired `/portal`.

Outside this PR: the SaaS checkout functions must accept `https://stirling.com/app/desktop/return` as a return URL, and hosted mode for credit bundles. Until then the browser does not hand back to the app after paying; returning to the window refreshes billing.

## How to test

Automated:
- `task frontend:check`
- `PW_DESKTOP=1 npx playwright test --project=stubbed-desktop desktop-processor` (in `frontend/editor`) boots the desktop build against stubbed self-hosted and Stirling Cloud servers. It opens the Processor, launches into it from the setting, and checks that local mode is sent back to the editor.

Manual, on a Windows build (`task desktop:build:dev:windows`):
1. Sign in to Stirling Cloud. The rail's Processor opens in the app; Settings shows Users and Usage & Billing; Add capacity opens checkout in the browser.
2. Sign in to a self-hosted server as its owner. Open the Processor, then Usage & Billing > Connect: sign in inside the app and the server links. Renew the sign-in once it lapses.
3. In local mode, the rail's Processor entry opens sign-in.
4. Set Settings > General > Default view on launch to Processor and restart.

Exercised so far on a Windows build: step 1 up to the checkout toast fixed in `12fc6fe0be` (not re-checked since). Steps 2 to 4, the Stripe deep-link return, and macOS/Linux have not been run end to end.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * The desktop app now includes the Processor, with access-aware navigation and an option to launch directly into it.
  * Added cloud sign-in, account linking, and team management.
  * Billing and checkout can open in a browser and return to the desktop app.

* **Improvements**
  * Settings navigation and search adapt to the current connection and access.
  * External links and file downloads use more consistent handling.
  * Desktop billing and checkout support browser-based payment flows.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved navigation, access checks, billing returns, and API request handling.

Fixes image signature sizing so signatures retain consistent PDF dimensions regardless of the viewer zoom level.

- Store image signature placement dimensions in PDF units instead of screen pixels.
- Scale the placement preview according to the current viewer zoom.
- Reuse a signature’s resized dimensions for subsequent placements.

issue.body:
Closes: #4223

Lets every split method name its output files: pages, chapters, sections, file size, page count, document count, page divider and printable chunks. Naming lives in its own **Advanced Settings** step, collapsed by default and shown once a method is chosen. It holds a **Name output files** dropdown, empty by default (each method keeps its own default names: bookmark titles for chapters, page and section numbers for sections, `filename_N` elsewhere):

- **Part 1, Part 2…**, **Chapter 1…**, **Section 1…**: presets, translated with the UI.
- **Custom pattern…**: a text field where `{n}` becomes the file number (`Invoice {n}` gives `Invoice 1.pdf`, `Invoice 2.pdf`…), with a live preview. A pattern without `{n}` has the number appended.
- **Type each name…**: one name per line, in order. A blank line, or a file beyond the list, keeps the default name.

A pattern works however many files the split produces, which the browser can't know ahead of time (split by size, chapters, page divider). That's why it is expanded on the server, not the client. Methods that produce a single file (sections with merge, printable chunks) give it the first name.

### API

Every split endpoint takes two optional fields, from a shared `SplitOutputNamingRequest` base:

- `outputNamePattern`: the name for every document, with `{n}` replaced by its 1-based number. It takes the place of the method's default name.
- `outputNames`: one name per line. Line N names document N, taking precedence over the pattern for that document.

`SplitOutputNames` hands out one name per document, so each controller keeps its own default. All names are sanitised (path separators, control characters, Windows reserved names, leading dots, a trailing `.pdf`, a 200-byte cap). They are de-duplicated ignoring case: a name the user typed keeps its exact form and the generated one takes a `_2`, `_3`… suffix. The frontend zip builder no longer drops an entry whose name repeats.

issue.body:
## Current state

The login-enabled chains (`SecurityConfiguration`, `SupabaseSecurityConfig`) permit a request when string checks in `RequestUriUtils` say it is a static asset, a public auth endpoint or a frontend route, and require a login for everything else. Since Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF#8617 those checks decode the path first, so for the cases we know about they agree with the path Spring MVC dispatches on.

## Problem

Whether an `/api/` handler can be reached anonymously still depends on every string check reading the path the same way the dispatcher does. Two places still don't:

- `isPublicAuthEndpoint` matches the OAuth callback segments anywhere in the path (`contains("/login/oauth2/code/")`, `contains("/oauth2/authorization/")`). An `/api/...` path ending in one of those is permitted by the chain and skipped by the auth filters. Nothing sensitive sits behind such a path today, but it is the same kind of mismatch, and the next catch-all API route would inherit it.
- `BillableOperationClassifier` prefix-tests the raw request URI, so an AI tool call whose path contains an escaped character reaches the AI handler but is metered as a manual (never billed) call.

## Solution

- **`PublicRouteRules`**, shared by both chains, orders the rules so a path is public because it is a known page, not because it fails to look like an API:
  1. the anchored public backend list (`RequestUriUtils.isPublicBackendEndpoint`: the `/api/` and `/actuator/health` entries split out of `isPublicAuthEndpoint`, unchanged, plus `/api/v1/info/status`);
  2. `/api/**` and `/actuator/**` require a login, matched by Spring's own `requestMatchers` (PathPattern, the same parsing the dispatcher uses);
  3. the existing static / public page / frontend-route checks.
- **`BillableOperationClassifier`** classifies by `HandlerMapping.BEST_MATCHING_PATTERN_ATTRIBUTE`, as `PaygChargeInterceptor`, `AiToolRoutes` and `PolicyRunRoutes` already do, with the decoded path as the fallback.

No change for well-formed requests: every `/api/` path that was public stays public (status, auth login/refresh/logout, login UI data, footer, invite validate/accept, mobile scanner, webhooks, workflow participant, share-link download, actuator health). The one visible difference is that a bare `/api` now answers 401 instead of serving the SPA shell.

Left alone on purpose:

- `FileStorage.enforceOwnership` still lets a request with no user through. Async job threads read files that way (the owner travels in `JobContext`, not the security context), and the HTTP entry point (`/files/{fileId}`) already runs `validateJobAccess`, which refuses owned keys without a user.
- `DeviceCredentialAuthenticationFilter.shouldNotFilter` still prefix-tests the raw URI. A mismatch there only skips the filter, which leaves the request unauthenticated.
- `isTrackableResource` / `MetricsFilter` use the raw URI for counting only; API counters are already keyed by the matched pattern.

## How to test

- `PublicRouteRulesHttpTest` sends raw escaped paths (`/%61pi/...`, `/a%70i/...`, `/%61ctuator/...`, a callback-suffixed API path) through a real Jetty server and checks public pages stay open. To confirm it has teeth I ran it against mutated code:
  - old rule shape, no decoding (pre-#8617): 6 of 7 backend cases fail
  - old rule shape, decoding (main today): 1 fails, the callback case
  - new rules, decoding removed from `normalizeUri`: all pass, so the matcher rule holds on its own
- Live, `SECURITY_ENABLELOGIN=true`: anonymous `GET`/`HEAD` on plain and escaped `/api/v1/info/load/all`, `/api/v1/general/job/{id}/result`, `/api/v1/config/app-config` answer 401; `/`, `/login`, `/files/abc`, `/processor`, `/share/{uuid}`, `/invite/{uuid}`, `/v1/api-docs`, `/actuator/health`, `/api/v1/info/status`, `/api/v1/ui-data/footer-info` answer 200; login, an async job and its download with a token still work.
- `ENABLE_SAAS=true ./gradlew spotlessCheck test`

# Description of Changes

- `pdftohtml` got the upload's base name as a bare positional argument, so a file named `-xml.pdf` / `-stdout.pdf` / `--help.pdf` was read as an option, a long name failed to convert, and the name was written unescaped into the generated HTML. It now always gets the fixed output name `document`, and the input path is absolute. The zip entries in the HTML and Markdown exports are now `document.html`, `document001.png` and so on; the zip itself keeps the upload's name.
- `processPdfToHtml` and `processPdfToOfficeFormat` no longer swallow zip write errors and return a broken zip as a success.
- The `/file/pdf` work dir and the PDF/A LibreOffice output dir now come from `TempFileManager`, so they use the configured temp location and are covered by the periodic cleanup.
- `/file/pdf` now closes the upload's input stream.
- `/convert/file/pdf`: the work dir is now deleted when the LibreOffice conversion or the sanitize step fails.
- `/convert/ebook/pdf`: the working dir (which holds the upload) is now deleted when Calibre fails, since the checks now run inside the try/finally.
- `/convert/pdf/pdfa` (PDFBox/LibreOffice fallback): the LibreOffice output dir is now deleted when the LibreOffice step fails.
- Audited every other `ProcessExecutor` command line (LibreOffice/unoconvert, calibre, gs, qpdf, tesseract/ocrmypdf, weasyprint, ffmpeg, magick, rar). None of them pass a user-controlled argument that can start with `-`: they use absolute temp paths, allowlisted values, or the `--opt=value` form.

Verified against the running backend (`bootRun`, host poppler 26.10 and calibre), before and after, with a generated one-page PDF:

| Request | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/pdf/html` `-xml.pdf` | 200, empty zip (22 B), `stirling-pdf-*.xml` left in the temp root | 200, zip with `document.html`, `document-1.html`, `document_ind.html`, `document001.png` |
| `/pdf/html` `-stdout.pdf` | 200, empty zip, 4 HTML/PNG files left in the temp root | 200, full zip |
| `/pdf/html` `--help.pdf` | 200, empty zip | 200, full zip |
| `/pdf/html` `-q -o x.pdf` / `normal.pdf` | full zip | full zip, entries named `document*` |
| `/file/pdf` with a failing LibreOffice stub | `office2pdf_` dir left behind | none left |
| `/ebook/pdf` with a corrupt `.epub` | working dir with the uploaded `.epub` left behind | none left |
| `/pdf/pdfa` (`pdfa-1`, Ghostscript unavailable) with a failing LibreOffice stub | `output_` dir left behind | none left |

- `/pdf/markdown` no longer uses `pdftohtml` (`PdfMarkdownExtractor`) and `/pdf/epub` passes absolute paths. Both returned correct output for all four names before and after.
- The fixed output name was checked against poppler 24.04 `pdftohtml`: both the HTML (`-c`) and Markdown (`-s -noframes -c`) commands write only `document*` files into the working dir, while a 250-character name fails with `Couldn't open html file`.

## HTML walkthrough

[pr-8500-setup-wizard-walkthrough.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33970153/pr-8500-setup-wizard-walkthrough.html)


# Description of Changes

The first admin to sign in to a new self-hosted server goes straight into a setup wizard instead of the old "change password, sign out, sign in again" sequence.

**Flow**
- **Sign-in:** a server still on the default `admin` / `stirling` login signs that admin in by itself and opens setup.
- **Account:** shown first when the admin is still on the default password. They choose a username and a new password, a "Details saved" toast confirms it, and they stay signed in: the server doesn't revoke their token, and the token is refreshed as setup closes.
- **First card:** Quick start or Custom. There is no skip: setup closes only once one of them is finished.
- **Quick start:** one summary card with the essentials at their defaults (web and server address, sign-in method, email, AI and MCP), then Analytics.
- **Custom:** one card per setting: addresses, language, sign-in, email, files, AI (with MCP), analytics.
- **Analytics:** starts on, and its button reads "Accept and continue" / "Decline and continue".
- Settings that open more fields (OAuth sign-in, SMTP, the AI engine, document questions) expand inside their own group, one at a time, with a chevron, and animate open and shut. The card has a max height: content scrolls and the button stays put.

**Saving**
- Only settings whose value differs from the server's are written, in one `PUT /api/v1/admin/settings`, then one restart. A server that can't restart itself (any non-JAR run, including Docker today) gets a "restart it yourself" card.
- An OAuth sign-in issuer must answer OIDC discovery before it's saved, via a new admin-only endpoint `POST /api/v1/admin/settings/check-issuer`. The issuer is saved and compared exactly as entered, so providers that advertise a trailing slash (Auth0) pass. The check refuses link-local addresses and the cloud metadata services, doesn't follow redirects, and reads at most 256 KB.
- MCP's OAuth mode now resolves its issuer on first use (`LazyIssuerJwtDecoder`), so an issuer that is down or mistyped no longer stops the server booting. Until it resolves, `/mcp` answers 401; discovery runs on one request at a time and a failed attempt waits 30 s before retrying.

**Showing it once**
- `system.setupCompleted` ships as `false` in the template for new servers, but defaults to `true` when absent: `ConfigInitializer` merges an existing `settings.yml` without the key as `true`, and a read-only one the migration can't write still binds as set up. Upgraded servers never see the wizard.
- Finishing sets it through `POST /api/v1/admin/settings/setup-complete`, which applies in memory before writing the file, so it sticks even if the write or the restart fails.

issue.body:
Closes: #4223

Lets every split method name its output files: pages, chapters, sections, file size, page count, document count, page divider and printable chunks. Naming lives in its own **Advanced Settings** step, collapsed by default and shown once a method is chosen. It holds a **Name output files** dropdown, empty by default (each method keeps its own default names: bookmark titles for chapters, page and section numbers for sections, `filename_N` elsewhere):

- **Part 1, Part 2…**, **Chapter 1…**, **Section 1…**: presets, translated with the UI.
- **Custom pattern…**: a text field where `{n}` becomes the file number (`Invoice {n}` gives `Invoice 1.pdf`, `Invoice 2.pdf`…), with a live preview. A pattern without `{n}` has the number appended.
- **Type each name…**: one name per line, in order. A blank line, or a file beyond the list, keeps the default name.

A pattern works however many files the split produces, which the browser can't know ahead of time (split by size, chapters, page divider). That's why it is expanded on the server, not the client. Methods that produce a single file (sections with merge, printable chunks) give it the first name.

### API

Every split endpoint takes two optional fields, from a shared `SplitOutputNamingRequest` base:

- `outputNamePattern`: the name for every document, with `{n}` replaced by its 1-based number. It takes the place of the method's default name.
- `outputNames`: one name per line. Line N names document N, taking precedence over the pattern for that document.

`SplitOutputNames` hands out one name per document, so each controller keeps its own default. All names are sanitised (path separators, control characters, Windows reserved names, leading dots, a trailing `.pdf`, a 200-byte cap). They are de-duplicated ignoring case: a name the user typed keeps its exact form and the generated one takes a `_2`, `_3`… suffix. The frontend zip builder no longer drops an entry whose name repeats.

issue.body:
**Summary**:
Allow Stirling-PDF Docker containers to run as arbitrary non-root users.
- Avoid running `chown` when the current user is not root.
- Fall back to the numeric UID when no username exists for the current user.

Resolves issue #1516 "_[Bug]: Running Stirling-PDF in docker with --user (rootless, unprivileged)_":
> the current way requiring PUID and PGID is not fitting those requirements, because it does not allow to run this container rootless.
> To run the container without root permissions, the following command should work:
> docker run -it --user 2000 frooodle/s-pdf:latest

---

**Description of Changes**:

`init.sh`:
- The initialization script assumes it has permission to run `chown`.
- `chown` exits with error `Operation not permitted`.
  - Only attempt ownership changes when running as root.
```bash
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  chown -R stirlingpdfuser:stirlingpdfgroup /tmp/stirling-pdf || true
fi
```

`init-without-ocr.sh`:
- The initialization script assumes the current UID has an associated username.
- `id` exits with error `no such user`.
  - Fall back to the numeric UID.
```bash
$(id -un 2>/dev/null || id -u)
```

---

**Notes**:
When running as a non-root user, some paths inside the container image are no longer writable.
Writable paths must be provided through mounts (volumes, tmpfs, etc.).

`init-without-ocr.sh`:
- Diagnostic helper symlinks are created in a populated root-owned directory `/usr/local/bin`.
- `ln` exits with error `Permission denied`.

I have an AI finding:

The repair try/catch falls back on an exception, but not on a repair that returns invalid bytes — which then fails the whole save instead of falling back to the valid unrepaired file. In exportToBlob, repairStructure is wrapped so a throw keeps the unrepaired bytes; but if it returns a non-null buffer that is malformed without throwing, bytes becomes that buffer and the later assertSavedPdf(bytes) (outside the catch) throws, so the export fails and the user cannot download their edit at all. The unrepaired bytes were a perfectly valid PDF (just with the duplicate MCIDs a UA validator dislikes — not a corrupt file), so failing the entire save over a cosmetic-for-non-UA-users repair is the harsher outcome. Since this pass now runs for every tagged-page text edit, consider re-validating the repaired bytes and falling back to the unrepaired (valid) save on failure, rather than letting a repair miscompute turn a good save into a failed one. The incremental-append design and the test suite make this unlikely, but the asymmetry is worth closing while repair is new.

issue.body:
## Summary

Sends MCP server usage to PostHog using PostHog's MCP analytics event names (`$mcp_*`), so the built-in PostHog MCP dashboard works for our Java MCP server.

Events:
- `$mcp_initialize` - client name/version, protocol version, server version
- `$mcp_tools_list` - tool names listed
- `$mcp_tool_call` - tool name, category, operation id, duration, error flag and error type
- `mcp_daily_users` - a daily count of distinct MCP users, split by auth method (API key vs OAuth)

## Privacy

- Never sends tool arguments, tool responses, free text or per-user identifiers. Events are captured with `$process_person_profile: false`.
- Distinct users are held in memory only and leave the server as counts.
- Tool errors are sent as a flag and type only (`tool_error` / `exception`); no error text is sent. Exceptions send only the exception class name.
- `stirling_operation` is only sent when the id exists in the operation catalog, so free text typed as an operation never leaves the server.
- Respects `system.enableAnalytics` and is checked on every call, so toggling analytics at runtime takes effect immediately.

## Implementation

- New `McpAnalytics` component (only active when `mcp.enabled=true`).
- `initialize` returns an `Mcp-Session-Id` header (random `ses_` id) so later tool calls can be tied to the client info. The session map is a bounded LRU (10k), best effort per node.
- The MCP auth filters set a request attribute with the auth method (`api_key` / `oauth`).
- Tools expose an `analyticsCategory()` for grouping.

## Testing

- `McpServerControllerTest` covers the events, properties, the analytics-disabled path, that tool error text is never sent and that non-catalog operation ids are dropped. Existing MCP integration tests are updated for the new constructor arg.

the tool-error message egress doesn’t match the PR’s own privacy claim. The body says error messages “are only sent when they match a safe token pattern,” but the tool_error branch does $mcp_error_message = redact(errorText(result)), and redact only takes the first line, blanks single-quoted substrings, and truncates to 200 chars — it never applies SAFE_TOKEN, and capture() doesn’t re-sanitize.
